overview: Switzerland is a landlocked country in Central Europe. Its federal capital is Bern, Zurich is its largest city, and Geneva hosts many international organisations, including the Red Cross and offices of the United Nations. Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. It has a long tradition of neutrality and is not a member of the European Union.

geography.text: The Alps cover about 60 percent of Switzerland, with famous peaks such as the Matterhorn and many glaciers. North of the Alps lies the Swiss Plateau, where most people live, and the Jura Mountains run along the border with France. Great rivers such as the Rhine and the Rhône begin in the Swiss Alps, and the country has large lakes, including Lake Geneva and Lake Constance.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Cold, snowy winters in the Alps and milder weather around the lakes.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Ibex, chamois, marmots and golden eagles live in the mountains.

history.text: Switzerland traces its beginnings to 1291, when three Alpine communities swore an alliance to defend each other, and over the centuries other cantons joined them. Its neutrality was recognised by Europe's great powers in 1815, and in 1848 it became a modern federal state. Switzerland stayed out of both World Wars and only joined the United Nations in 2002.

events.title: The first alliance
events.text: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swear to defend each other.

events.title: Battle of Marignano
events.text: A heavy defeat leads the Swiss to step back from European wars.

events.title: Neutrality recognised
events.text: The great powers recognise Swiss neutrality.

events.title: Votes for women
events.text: Women gain the right to vote in national elections.

events.title: Joins the UN
events.text: Switzerland becomes a member of the United Nations.

government.text: Switzerland is a federal republic of 26 cantons. It has no single head of state: the country is led by a seven-member Federal Council, and its presidency rotates every year. Swiss voters decide many issues directly in referendums several times a year. Switzerland is neutral and is not in the European Union or NATO.

economy.text: Switzerland is one of the richest countries in the world. It is famous for banking, watches, chocolate and cheese, and for global companies in medicine and food, such as Roche, Novartis and Nestlé. It uses its own currency, the Swiss franc.

culture.text: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. It is home to the Red Cross, founded in Geneva in 1863, and to many international organisations. Swiss inventions include Velcro and the Swiss Army knife.

items.title: Four languages
items.text: German, French, Italian and Romansh are all national languages.

items.title: The Matterhorn
items.text: A 4,478-metre peak on the border with Italy.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Cheese fondue, raclette and Swiss chocolate.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Swiss graphic design and typography, including the Helvetica typeface, influenced the world.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: In spring, cows are taken up to mountain pastures decorated with flowers and bells, and brought down again in autumn.

sport.text: Skiing is a national passion, and Switzerland has won many Olympic medals in Alpine skiing. Roger Federer, one of the greatest tennis players of all time, is Swiss. FIFA and the International Olympic Committee both have their headquarters in Switzerland.

items.title: Roger Federer
items.text: Won 20 Grand Slam titles, including eight Wimbledons.
St. Moritz hosted the Winter Olympics twice.

items.title: IOC
items.text: The International Olympic Committee is based in Lausanne.

didYouKnow: Switzerland has enough nuclear shelters for its whole population.
The World Wide Web was invented at CERN, near Geneva, in 1989.

keyPeople.name: Henri Dunant
keyPeople.text: Won the first Nobel Peace Prize, in 1901.

keyPeople.name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
keyPeople.text: Born in Geneva; his ideas inspired the French Revolution.
